classification.difficultyReason: Link graphs of two familiar linear equations with their intersection, including exact fractional arithmetic.

content.prompt: For each pair of equations, sketch the graphs and find the coordinates of the point of intersection.

answer.worked:
Plot $(0,1)$ and $(1,4)$ for $y=3x+1$, and $(0,2)$ and $(1,4)$ for $y=2x+2$. Draw both lines on the same axes. They intersect at $(1,4)$.

At the intersection:
$$\begin{align*}3x+1&=2x+2\\x&=1\\y&=3(1)+1\\y&=4\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Both equations plotted on common numbered axes; dashed styling distinguishes the second line.

answer.worked:
Plot $(0,3)$ and $(2,-1)$ for $y=3-2x$, and $(0,-3)$ and $(3,0)$ for $y=x-3$. Draw both lines on the same axes. They intersect at $(2,-1)$.

At the intersection:
$$\begin{align*}3-2x&=x-3\\6&=3x\\x&=2\\y&=2-3\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$

Plot $(0,1)$ and $(1,3)$ for $y=2x+1$, and $(0,3)$ and $(-1,-2)$ for $y=5x+3$. Draw both lines on the same axes.

Find the exact intersection as in Example 14:
$$\begin{align*}2x+1&=5x+3\\-2&=3x\\x&=-\frac23\\y&=2\left(-\frac23\right)+1\\y&=-\frac13\end{align*}$$
The intersection is $\left(-\frac23,-\frac13\right)$.
